title: Xanthe and the Parish
premise: When the coffin of Xanthe Parish, founder of the river town of Ashmoor, is exhumed for a centenary reburial and found empty, retired detective Casper Brightwater is dragged back into the work he fled twelve years ago. The trail leads to Nell Voss, a woman officially dead since 2013 who has been living in plain sight as the parish archivist, and to the town's ruling families, whose fortunes were built on a drowning Casper was paid to misfile. As Casper closes in on Nell — and on his own complicity — he must choose between protecting the lie that keeps Ashmoor solvent and exposing the truth that will destroy it. In the end, Nell surrenders herself at the centenary ceremony, Casper testifies against the families, and the bookshop burns with every secret file inside.
about_author: Theo Ashgrove is the pen name of a former small-town newspaper editor who spent a decade covering municipal scandals in river towns before turning to fiction. They live near water, keep meticulous files, and insist none of their novels are about anywhere real.

chapters.title: The Weight of Paper
chapters.summary: Casper Brightwater's POV. A slow morning in Brightwater Books: dusting spines, alphabetizing a private drawer of case files he swore he'd never reopen. Establishes his routine, his tremor, his guilt. Beat: uneasy calm before disruption.

chapters.title: Exhumation Order
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The historical society wins approval to move Xanthe Parish's remains for the centenary reburial. Councilman Aldous Fenwick asks Casper, casually, to attend. Casper notices the request isn't casual. Beat: dread disguised as civic pride.

chapters.title: Empty
chapters.summary: Cemetery scene, Casper's POV. The vault is opened before forty witnesses: no coffin, no body, only a cavity of clean river clay. Gasps, cameras, Aldous's face going gray. Casper recognizes professional removal when he sees one. Beat: shock.

chapters.title: The Man Who Used to Know Things
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Sheriff Ilsa Marsh visits the bookshop — not to hire him, but to warn him off. He accepts the warning and immediately begins pulling his old files. Introduce the 2013 drowning of Tom Voss, ruled accidental. Beat: relapse into obsession.

chapters.title: A Woman Made of Ink
chapters.summary: Nell Voss's POV, unnamed. She works late in the parish archive, burning selected pages from the centenary records. She knows the grave was opened; she planned for it years ago. Beat: cold competence, hidden identity.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Alphabetical Silence
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Flashback woven through present: the night in 2013 he took money from the Fenwick family to close the Voss file. His wife left over it; the bookshop was bought with the remainder. Beat: self-loathing surfacing.

chapters.title: The Archivist Who Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. He interviews parish staff about records missing from 2013. The archivist, 'Miss Vale,' is helpful, forgettable, gone by the time he looks up. Readers may glimpse what Casper misses. Beat: dramatic irony.

chapters.title: River Clay
chapters.summary: Ilsa Marsh's POV. Forensics date the grave's disturbance to roughly a decade ago — someone emptied it long ago and let the town venerate an absence. Ilsa suspects the exhumation was engineered. Beat: the mystery deepens.

chapters.title: Fenwick House
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Dinner at the Fenwick estate. Aldous offers Casper a consulting fee to find 'who desecrated' the grave. Casper reads the offer as containment, not investigation, and takes it anyway — access is access. Beat: moral compromise renewed.

chapters.title: The Drowning File
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. He reconstructs Tom Voss's death: a surveyor who found discrepancies in the flood-levee contracts, drowned two days before signing an affidavit. Casper's own signature closed the case. Beat: guilt made concrete.

chapters.title: Miss Vale's Hours
chapters.summary: Nell's POV. She observes Casper in the archive, testing whether he remembers her face from 2013 — she was Tom's wife, presumed drowned with him. She decides he's the only honest instrument available. Beat: predator choosing a tool.

chapters.title: What the Levee Hid
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Old blueprints show the levee was deliberately underbuilt to flood Voss land cheaply; four founding families profited. The same families now fund the centenary. Beat: conspiracy takes shape.

chapters.title: A Threat, Politely Worded
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. His shop window is smashed; inside, a centenary invitation with 'ALPHABETIZE THIS' scrawled across it. He reports nothing. First time in twelve years he feels awake. Beat: fear braided with exhilaration.

chapters.title: The Witness List
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. She finds the original affidavit unsigned but witnessed — by a notary whose stamp matches documents still flowing through the parish office. Someone dead has been notarizing papers for a decade. Beat: uncanny clue.

chapters.title: Dead Women Don't Renew Licenses
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. He traces the notary license renewal to a PO box and a handwriting sample that makes his blood run cold: Nell Voss, alive, or someone very good at being her. Beat: revelation.

chapters.title: Ashes in the Stacks
chapters.summary: Nell's POV. She discovers someone else is also destroying records — not her. A second hand in the archive. She realizes the families are erasing ahead of the centenary too. Beat: rival conspiracies collide.

chapters.title: The Bookshop at Night
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. An intruder searches his files; Casper interrupts and fights a figure who escapes, leaving behind a 2013 photograph of Tom, Nell, and — unmistakably — a younger Casper at the river. Beat: personal stakes ignite.

chapters.title: Confession, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. He goes to Ilsa to confess his 2013 bribe. Before he can speak, she shows him a warrant naming HIM as a person of interest in the grave tampering. Someone framed him first. Beat: trap closing.

chapters.title: Run, Detective
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Half the town saw him at the cemetery after hours; the Fenwicks have the narrative. He skips town briefly, following the PO box to a river houseboat registered to a dead man. Beat: fugitive paranoia.

chapters.title: The Houseboat
chapters.summary: Nell's POV. She returns to the houseboat and finds evidence Casper has been there — and leaves a message for him instead of a trap: coordinates, a time, and one word: 'testify.' Beat: gambit.

chapters.title: Two Liars at a Table
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Casper meets Nell at a shuttered cannery. She lays out everything: the levee fraud, Tom's murder, her faked death, her decade gathering proof. She needs his testimony about the bribe. He needs absolution. Neither trusts the other. Beat: uneasy alliance.

chapters.title: What Nell Buried
chapters.summary: Nell's POV. Her backstory: she watched the families drown her husband's truth, so she drowned herself instead — literally staged it, then became Miss Vale to sit beside the evidence for ten years. The empty grave was her deadline mechanism. Beat: tragic resolve.

chapters.title: The Second Hand
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Together they identify the other record-destroyer: Aldous's son Marcus Fenwick, quietly sanitizing the family paper trail. But Marcus is also skimming from his father — he might be turned. Beat: leverage found.

chapters.title: Buying a Fenwick
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper confronts Marcus with evidence of embezzlement and offers immunity-shaped silence in exchange for the family's private correspondence. Marcus wavers, then hands over a single letter signed by all four families. Beat: betrayal within betrayal.

chapters.title: The Letter
chapters.summary: Nell's POV. The 2013 letter authorizes 'permanent resolution of the Voss inconvenience.' It names the four signatories — including the beloved town matriarch, Odile Crane, centenary chairwoman. Nell finally has the chain of command. Beat: triumph shadowed by grief.

chapters.title: Odile Crane Serves Tea
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Summoned to tea with Odile, Casper expects threat and gets something worse: genuine warmth, and an offer — leave town, debts forgiven, a pension. She speaks of Ashmoor like a body she keeps alive. Beat: seduction of complicity.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. He walks the town seeing what the hush-money built: the clinic, the school roof, the levee repairs — all funded by the settlement. Exposing the families ruins more than them. Beat: thematic crisis.

chapters.title: Marcus Regrets
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Marcus, panicking, contacts Ilsa anonymously; she traces the call and realizes the case is real and enormous. She chooses, quietly, to stop hunting Casper and start hunting the families. Beat: ally converted.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Nell's POV. The families find Nell first. She escapes the archive as it burns — decades of parish records, hers and theirs, gone. She saves only the letter and her own sworn statement. Beat: loss and narrowing odds.

chapters.title: Ashes of the Archive
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Fire investigation points to arson; suspicion falls conveniently on Nell. Casper realizes the fire destroys HIS corroboration too — without the archive, it's his word against dynasties. Beat: despair.

chapters.title: One Honest Cop
chapters.summary: Casper and Ilsa, shared scene. In her kitchen, Casper gives a full recorded confession of the 2013 bribe. Ilsa warns him it ends his life either way. He says he's been dead twelve years already. Beat: redemption committed to.

chapters.title: The Centenary Begins
chapters.summary: Multiple brief POVs. Banners, brass band, four families on the reviewing stand, a coffin-sized monument waiting for remains that don't exist. Nell moves through the crowd in plain clothes, unremarkable. Beat: held breath.

chapters.title: What Rises from the Grave
chapters.summary: Climax part one, Casper's POV. At the reburial ceremony, Casper takes the microphone uninvited and tells the town everything: the levee, the murder, the bribe, his own signature. Uproar; Aldous orders him seized. Beat: public detonation.

chapters.title: Nell Voss, Living
chapters.summary: Climax part two, Nell's POV. As guards drag Casper off, Nell walks to the monument, holds up the letter and her notary seal, and announces herself: 'You buried me once. It didn't take.' The crowd recognizes Tom Voss's widow. Beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: The Families Break
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. With the town watching, arrests begin. Odile doesn't run; she corrects Ilsa's paperwork with terrifying courtesy. Marcus confesses fully, trading on his cooperation. One family patriarch collapses at the podium. Beat: reckoning.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Deposition room. Casper testifies to his own crime in exhaustive detail, refusing every softening. The prosecutor offers him a deal; he declines partial truth. Beat: penance performed.

chapters.title: Sentencing
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper receives eighteen months; Nell receives probation and a hero's ambivalence — half the town calls her savior, half calls her arsonist. The levee contracts are voided; federal engineers arrive. Beat: justice, imperfect.

chapters.title: The Fire That Casper Set
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Confession within confession: before surrendering, Casper burned his own drawer of misfiled cases — including others he'd buried for pay. Nell listens without judgment. Two people who falsified the past, facing it together. Beat: full honesty.

chapters.title: Inventory
chapters.summary: Nell's POV. Closing the bookshop for his sentence, Casper and Nell catalog what remains. She takes a job rebuilding the parish archive honestly. He asks her to write while he's away. Quiet, almost tender. Beat: hope earned.

chapters.title: Xanthe and the Parish
chapters.summary: Epilogue, letters between Casper and Nell. Eighteen months later he returns to a town still arguing with its history, a rebuilt archive, and a shop reopened under both their names. The monument bears a new plaque: 'For everyone the parish failed.' Final line: some files should stay open. Beat: resolution and renewal.
